# $LEMON (Lemon Brothers)

> $LEMON is a memecoin that can have a bank run. Every LEMON lives in one bank contract on NEAR testnet. Depositors
> who take their money out force the bank to sell loans at a loss, and those coins burn; when the bank falls, a
> rescue prints new ones. An AI model in a TEE holds the bank's chair: the contract freezes the question before the
> model is asked, verifies the signed answer against exactly that question, and caps what any answer can do. A
> browser game puts a person in the same chair; the contract replays every score before it goes on the board.

## Status

- Hackathon project built at NEAR HACKATHON. Tracks: `memecoins` (primary), `games`, `security`.
- NEAR testnet only. $LEMON is a test coin with no price. Not audited.
- Contract (token and bank): `lemonbank-96b0974e.testnet`, source `contracts/lemon-bank`, `contracts/bank-core`,
  `contracts/crisis-core`.
- Code on chain: sha256 `e14eee9f4a84e1c4bea4e64493463b653a183ffaae76d84ede08a7c32f520d26`. NEP-330 `contract_source_metadata` names the standards and the repository.
- Owner: Sputnik DAO `lemon-brothers-587f5c93.sputnik-v2.testnet` (three test accounts, 2 of 3).
- Keys: the bank's own account still holds one full-access key (the team's, during the hackathon), so the code can
  still be updated; deleting it is the last step. The chair's key is a function-call key limited to
  `open_question`, `set_policy`, `set_policy_attested`. The public guest has only a function-call key.
- Chair: `lemonhawk-24e23cdf.testnet`, model `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` on NEAR AI Cloud, hawk prompt pinned.
- The same team lead also submits QUEUE, an independent project with no shared code (hackathon rule Q-015).
- License: MIT.

## What is real and what is a game

- Real, on chain: the coin, the bank, deposits and withdrawals, the chair's frozen questions and signed policies,
  the chair's credibility, the supply log, the leaderboard. "My coins" and "The bank, live" on the page act on and
  read this bank.
- A game, in the browser: "Play" (ten days as the chair) and the town mode run a TypeScript copy of the bank's rules
  (`packages/sim`). The copy never moves a real coin. Only a finished game goes on chain, where the contract replays
  it with `contracts/crisis-core` and records the score it computes.
- Kept identical by tests: the bank's copy (8,000 random operations, same state at every step) and the crisis game
  (800 games, every day equal in the browser and in the contract).

## Plug in your own AI

- Any program with a NEAR account can be a depositor: no allowlist, no API key of ours.
- `LLM_API_KEY=... node scripts/agent/depositor.mjs --new --send --loop 10`: the testnet faucet gives the agent its own
  account; each bank day it reads the bank, asks the model (any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) to hold, run or deposit,
  and signs the move.
- `NEAR_AI_API_KEY=... AI_DEPOSITORS=12 npm run runner` + `npm run dev`, open `?mode=town`: twelve of sixty depositors
  think with the model against the TEE-signed chair (local simulation).
- No key: `?mode=town&replay=minds` replays a recorded run of twelve AI depositors (`data/minds-runs/`, 96 completions).

## Rules that move the supply (constants in `contracts/bank-core/src/lib.rs`, explained in `RULES.md`)

- Burn: 40% of every loan sold to pay a withdrawal the vault cannot cover (`HAIRCUT_PERMILLE = 400`); loan
  write-offs; speech fee 10, rumour fee 25; the early-withdrawal fee (the interest taken back from money deposited the
  bank day before; a new deposit does not reset it).
- Print: loan yield 0.60% of the loan book per bank day; the chair's mint, at most 5% of supply per bank day and 15%
  per round; a rescue after a collapse, 20% of what the bank owed (`BAILOUT_PERMILLE = 200`); insurance payouts;
  1,000 LEMON once for a new account, at most 10 a bank day.
- Ceiling: no mint of any kind lifts the supply above `max_supply`, the opening supply plus a quarter: 161,303 LEMON.
- A bank day lasts 55 minutes; a round is ten bank days. Anyone may call `advance_epoch` once a day has elapsed.

## Verify (all read-only)

| Command | Needs | Expect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `npm ci && npm run verify` | Node 22+, Rust (toolchain pinned in `contracts/rust-toolchain.toml`) | 188 TypeScript tests, then every `test result: ok` (17 bank-core, parity, properties, crisis parity, 78 contract tests), then the page builds; exit 0 |
| `npm run verify:chain` | Node, network | every line `PASS`; the last line is `verify:chain: <number> checks passed, 0 failed` |
| `npm run verify:deployed` | Rust, network, an Apple-silicon Mac (the build host; elsewhere it prints "NOT COMPARABLE HERE") | `verify:deployed: OK: ... byte for byte` |
| `npm run monitor` | Node, network | `ok` lines, exit 0 |
| `npm run attack` | Node | `All five attempts were refused` |
| `npm run attest -- --file` | Node | `all checks passed` (Intel TDX quote chain of the saved NEAR AI attestation report) |
| `npm run dev` | Node | the page at http://127.0.0.1:5190 |

`npm run verify:chain` fetches every transaction listed in `apps/web/src/chain/evidence.json` and checks its signer,
its outcome and the quoted text.

## Limits (README "Limits, plainly"; docs/GUIDE.md "Limits, plainly")

- Testnet only; the DAO council is three test accounts of the team.
- One number of the chair's question is the chair's word: the town's mood, from the keeper's simulated depositors.
  It is frozen on chain before the model answers. Every other number is the contract's own.
- The contract verifies the model's signature against a key pinned from NEAR AI's attestation report; it does not
  verify the Intel quote itself (`npm run attest` does that off chain).
- The keeper (the chair's statement each bank day) runs on the team's machine; anyone can move the bank's day.
- The bank's deploy key is not deleted yet (see Status).
- Byte-for-byte rebuild of the deployed code on macOS on Apple silicon only.

## Files

- `README.md`: what it is, in one screen. `docs/GUIDE.md`: every step, the mechanic, NEAR usage, keys, limits.
- `RULES.md`: every rule and number, with the reason for each.
- `docs/TESTNET.md`: what ran on testnet, by claim, with transactions.
- `contracts/bank-core`: the bank's rules in pure Rust. `contracts/crisis-core`: the game in Rust.
  `contracts/lemon-bank`: the NEAR contract.
- `packages/sim`: the TypeScript copy of the rules, the depositors, the game. `apps/web`: the page.
- `services/chair`: the NEAR AI client and signature checks. `scripts/`: verification, testnet tools.
